Rescue is genuinely slow. There is no cell coverage, the peak is in Whatcom County but your road access is in British Columbia, and the area sees only a handful of parties a year.
Wildfire regularly threatens access - the Border 2 Fire burned 2.4 km east of Hozomeen and crossed into B.C. in July 2026, closing the only road.

The rock is very good granite underneath but heavily lichened, and face and foot edges are brittle enough that they need testing and often break — do not trust a hold you have not weighted deliberately.
Cracks are packed with sand and loose flakes and need cleaning before jams stick; everything you clean falls on your belayer, so wear helmets and build belays out of the fall line where possible.
The face is essentially vertical and the pitch-3 crux traverses left on poor feet — a fall there swings, so manage rope drag and belayer position accordingly.
There is no fixed gear anywhere on the route. A retreat means leaving your own cams, and there is nothing to clip if you are caught out.
The last water is Upper Eagle Lake, 900-1,000 ft below the base. There is none on the face and none on the summit ridge.
Afternoon thunderstorms build over Sawtooth Ridge in July and August; you are on a vertical east-facing wall with no shelter and a metal rack.
The East Face loses the sun by mid-afternoon and gets cold fast even in August — a stalled party gets cold as well as late.
The descent is an unroped Class 2-3 scramble with a couple of Class 3 moves and 1,330 ft of loss; with snow on it, or in the dark, it is more dangerous than the climb.
This route has seen almost no traffic since 2011, so the grades, the pitch lengths and the line itself are one party's report — not a consensus you can lean on.
Wildfire closures have shut the Crater Creek trailhead in past seasons; check Okanogan-Wenatchee alerts before committing to the drive.
